prompt: You are painting a leaf. Which two paint colours can you mix together to make green?
explanation: In paint, blue and yellow are primary colours that mix to make green — the classic colour-mixing rule every painter learns first.
ageGuidance: Ages 3-8; a colour-mixing question for young painters, best tried afterwards with real paint and a grown-up.
materials: No materials needed to answer; optional afterwards: blue and yellow paint, paper and a brush
supervision: A grown-up should supervise any follow-up painting and hand-washing.
safetyNotes: Use child-safe, non-toxic washable paints only.
Cover clothes and tables before painting; wash hands afterwards.
screenFreeExtension: Mix blue and yellow paint on paper and paint the biggest leaf you can — then try adding a tiny bit more blue or yellow to change the green.
